references.text: The story of Jacob taking Leah and Rachel as wives, and how he hated Leah, illustrates the same theme of a man taking a wife and then hating her.
Samson took a Philistine woman as his wife, an example of a marriage that led to conflict and problems.
Samson visited his wife, but her father had given her to another, showing the complexity in marital relationships.
Laws regarding divorce when a man finds something indecent about his wife, related to the situation where a man hates his wife.
The law concerning taking a captive woman as a wife and what happens if the man no longer delights in her.
Malachi speaks of faithlessness toward one's wife and that the Lord hates divorce, relevant to the theme of marital conflict.
Jesus' teaching on divorce and adultery, which expands on the Old Testament laws concerning marriage.
Jesus discusses divorce with the Pharisees and refers to the Mosaic Law, including provisions about sending away one's wife.
